feature1.prompt: The Django admin currently fails to correctly display Unicode characters in JSONFields. When a JSONField contains Chinese or other non-ASCII characters, the default serialization using json.dumps results in escape sequences (for example, '\u4e2d\u56fd' instead of the actual characters). The goal is to modify the admin display so that the output shows the intended Unicode characters rather than their ASCII representations. This change will improve the readability of JSON data in the Django admin interface.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves modifying the admin display logic for JSONFields to ensure proper Unicode serialization. Developers should update the code so that json.dumps is invoked with the flag ensure_ascii set to False. This will guarantee that any JSON value rendered in the admin interface preserves its Unicode characters. Focus your efforts on the admin utilities that format JSONField output.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/contrib/admin/utils.py; Function: display_for_field. Locate the code block checking for instances of a JSONField and update the serialization call from field.get_prep_value(value) to json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, cls=field.encoder).

feature2.prompt: JSON data prepared for form fields also suffers from improper Unicode handling. The default behavior of json.dumps leads to the serialization of Unicode characters into ASCII escape sequences, which makes the output less human-readable. The intended improvement is to serialize JSON values for form fields in such a way that Unicode characters are preserved. This change will ensure that forms which handle JSON data display values with correct Unicode representations.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature focuses on updating how JSON data is prepared for Django form fields. The modification should take place in the method that calls json.dumps within the form field logic, ensuring the flag ensure_ascii is set to False. This adjustment will allow JSON values containing Unicode characters to appear correctly in forms. Developers should verify that the change is consistent with the intended behavior across the system.
feature2.entrypoint: File: django/forms/fields.py; Function: prepare_value. Locate the call to json.dumps and modify it so that it includes ensure_ascii=False along with the existing encoder parameter (cls=self.encoder).

collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Ensure that the changes in both the admin display and form field preparation use a unified approach to JSON serialization by consistently setting ensure_ascii to False. Code reviews and integration tests should verify that JSON data appears correctly in both contexts, reinforcing consistent behavior across the project.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on each feature should discuss the overall strategy for handling Unicode in JSON serialization. They must coordinate on the usage of common resources (like the encoder) and agree on how edge cases involving Unicode characters are managed in both the admin and form contexts.
